comments.value:
In 2021.3.1, we made some (pretty sweeping!) network changes that should help mitigate or prevent this issue entirely.
We haven't observed this issue ourselves, nor have we seen verifiable reports of the issue since the release. As such, I'm marking this as Complete.
**Notably, this is the issue we've addressed:** In a given instance with a number of users present, one or more users would eventually begin to exhibit IK "slideshowing", where IK update rate would slow down a lot and interpolation between IK updates would break or only have one interim step. This behavior would be observed by everyone in the instance on the same person-- in other words, if Person A was in this failure state, Persons B, C, D, etc would *all* see the behavior.
If you are observing other IK issues but they do not match the above description, *please create a new Feedback post.*

details:
Occasionally, when using 1053, other players have jerky movement, as if their movements aren't being interpolated. This affects individual users, and only after spending some time (tens of minutes) in the same instance.
Thus far, due in part to how it takes quite some time to repro, I've only reproed this with live users; while it's possible that this is a live incompatibility, given that this only affects a subset of users in the instance - and appears to be a lack of interpolation rather than problems with the IK data being received - it may be a bug in the beta itself.
Sample video showing this behaviour: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=06goAXvf-Kc
title: [1053] Occasional jerky player movement when testing on live
